y1: Jesus moved to the village of Capernaum by the Sea of Galilee.
y2: He began to spread the Gospel to the people: “Repent! The kingdom of heaven is near!” A great light dawned on the people who were in darkness.
y4: As Jesus was walking by the sea, He saw two brothers who were fishermen casting a net. They were Simon Peter and Andrew.
y5: Jesus said, “Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.” They immediately left their nets and followed Jesus.
y7: Going a little farther, Jesus saw two brothers, James and John, in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets.
y8: When Jesus called them, they immediately left the boat and their father and followed Him. Thus they became Jesus' first disciples.
y10: Jesus traveled all over Galilee, teaching about the kingdom of God and healing the sick.
y11: This news spread everywhere, and very large crowds followed Him.
verse: “Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.”
prayer: Jesus, thank You for calling me just as You called ordinary fishermen to be Your disciples. Help me to follow You with joy. Let my friends and family know You too. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: Sea of Galilee. It is a large lake in northern Israel. Many fishermen lived there because it had a lot of fish. Jesus called His disciples by the Sea of Galilee.
d1: Gospel. It means “good news.” It is the news that Jesus came to save us. Jesus spread the Gospel in every village.
d2: net. It is a tool woven tightly from ropes to catch fish. Peter and Andrew left their nets and followed Jesus.
d3: fisherman. A person who makes a living by catching fish. Jesus' first disciples were fishermen.
d4: follow. To go after someone, learn from them, and live like them. The disciples followed Jesus.
d5: disciple. A person who follows a teacher and learns from them. Jesus called twelve disciples.
d6: heal. To make a sick body or heart well. Jesus healed many people.
